title: Sheaf dg modules, localization, and derived extension notation
statement:
Fix universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be a topological space and $\mathcal S$ a sheaf of commutative rings. A sheaf dg $\mathcal S$-algebra is an integer cochain complex $\mathcal C$ of $\mathcal S$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with $\mathcal S$-bilinear associative unital multiplication and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^{|a|}a\,d(b)$. A left sheaf dg $\mathcal C$-module is a complex $M$ of $\mathcal S$-module sheaves with a unital associative $\mathcal S$-bilinear action satisfying $d(am)=d(a)m+(-1)^{|a|}a\,d(m)$. Maps are action-preserving degree-zero chain maps. A degree $r$ graded module map $h:M\to N$ is a family of $\mathcal S$-linear sheaf maps $h^i:M^i\to N^{i+r}$ with $h(am)=(-1)^{r|a|}a\,h(m)$. Write $K_X(\mathcal C)$ for the category with these modules as objects and maps modulo $f-g=d_Nh+hd_M$ for such a degree $-1$ map $h$. Let $W$ be its maps inducing isomorphisms on all underlying cohomology sheaves. Define $Q_{\mathcal C}:K_X(\mathcal C)\to D_X(\mathcal C)=K_X(\mathcal C)[W^{-1}]$ by formally adjoining inverses to $W$: morphisms are finite composable words in arrows and formal inverses, modulo the composition, identity and inverse relations, in the chosen larger universe. Underlying cohomology sheaves and $D(\mathcal S)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal S))$ use [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Use $M[k]^i=M^{i+k}$, $d_{M[k]}=(-1)^k d_M$, and shifted left action $a\cdot_{M[k]}m=(-1)^{k|a|}am$. For $f:M\to N$, its cone is $N\oplus M[1]$ with differential $(n,m)\mapsto(d_Nn+f(m),-d_Mm)$ and componentwise action using the shifted action on $M[1]$. The specified cone triangles are $M\xrightarrow f N\xrightarrow i C(f)\xrightarrow{-p}M[1]$, with inclusion $i(n)=(n,0)$ and projection $p(n,m)=m$, and their isomorphic images, using the signed convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and triangle notation of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Forgetting the action sends a word to the corresponding word of underlying chain maps and inverses in $D(\mathcal S)$; this defines the forgetful functor. For $M\in D_X(\mathcal C)$, locally perfect over $\mathcal C$ means that on some open cover $X=\bigcup U_\alpha$, its restriction lies in the smallest full subcategory of $D_{U_\alpha}(\mathcal C|_{U_\alpha})$ closed under isomorphisms, finite sums, shifts, cones and direct summands and containing the regular module $\mathcal C|_{U_\alpha}$. A direct summand here is a retract: there are maps $L\xrightarrow i P\xrightarrow r L$ with $ri=1_L$. Restrictions are restriction of the sheaves and all their structure maps.

For an $\mathcal S$-linear degree-zero chain map $\varphi:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C'$ preserving multiplication and the unit, restriction keeps the complex and restricts its action. The ordinary extension $\mathcal C'\otimes_{\mathcal C}M$ is the sheafified balanced direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], quotient by $(b\varphi(c))\otimes m=b\otimes cm$, with differential $d(b\otimes m)=d(b)\otimes m+(-1)^{|b|}b\otimes d(m)$ and left $\mathcal C'$-action on the first factor. Let $F$ denote ordinary extension and $\overline F=Q_{\mathcal C'}F:K_X(\mathcal C)\to D_X(\mathcal C')$. Write $\mathcal C'\otimes_{\mathcal C}^{\mathbf L}-$ for a functor $LF:D_X(\mathcal C)\to D_X(\mathcal C')$ equipped with a natural comparison $\epsilon:LF\circ Q_{\mathcal C}\Rightarrow\overline F$ having the following universal property: for every functor $V:D_X(\mathcal C)\to D_X(\mathcal C')$, composition with $\epsilon$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Nat}(V,LF)\simeq\operatorname{Nat}(V\circ Q_{\mathcal C},\overline F)$. This notation is used whenever such data exist. For a sheaf dg $\mathcal C'$-module $N$, the specified action counit is the composite $LF(Q_{\mathcal C}\operatorname{Res}N)\xrightarrow{\epsilon_{\operatorname{Res}N}}Q_{\mathcal C'}(\mathcal C'\otimes_{\mathcal C}\operatorname{Res}N)\to Q_{\mathcal C'}N$, whose second map is induced by $b\otimes n\mapsto bn$. These sentences define the notation and the specified map; they do not assert existence of the derived functor.

source.place: Tags 0FRF (definition-dga), 0FRI (definition-dgm), 0FT5 (definition-derived-category), 0FS5 (definition-cone); section-shift and definition-pullback. The source defaults to right modules; the displayed left convention includes the Koszul sign on shifts. Local perfectness is the explicit finite-generation-under-operations convention, not a finiteness theorem.

This is stable pointed-curve extension, not stable modification of a specified target pair. Moduli prerequisite: projective compactification with prime-to-characteristic level structure and its universal stable family, used before taking the closure of a generic lift. Knudsen forgetful morphism as the universal stable curve. Section 1, Theorem 1.8, Corollaries 1.9 and 1.11; Section 2, Proposition 2.1 (printed pp.172--175): degree-zero logarithmic components and their section-algebra contraction. Independent prerequisite: Cohomology and log dualizing comparison for a given elementary nodal contraction. Logarithmic comparison before Knudsen Lemma 1.6: generic coherent-duality trace on a perfect marking ideal, replacing the differential-dual presentation by the same adjunction-normalized relative duality. Prerequisite for the perfect-image coherent trace comparison: locality on affine opens for the proper map between the two curve families, without asserting that this map is flat. Independent prerequisite: Pseudo-coherent perfect direct images between flat finitely presented families. Kiehl finiteness input: the unnumbered general relative-pseudo-coherence assertion following Stacks lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general. Finite-degree Noetherian descente input for the Kiehl finiteness assertion. Independent prerequisite: Relative sheaf descente on a prescribed Noetherian envelope. Two-open gluing prerequisite, conditional on approximation on both opens and their intersection, uniform in a supplied finite coefficient stage. Single-degree induction step: cancel finite polynomial-chart top obstructions globally while retaining the prescribed scalar-action normalization. Mayer--Vietoris subproblem for one degree: given a global coherent witness at cutoff n+1 and witnesses on two opens at cutoff n, obtain a global witness at cutoff n. The supplied global witness is part of the hypothesis. Independent input: Sheaf dg coefficient realizations and normalized arrows. Second paragraph: sheaf dg modules, their localization, shifts, cones and perfectness; third and fourth paragraphs: derived extension and its action counit.

There is no repair note for this item, and the side-live item is still unsplit, so it is not superseded. No clause or hypothesis was dropped and none was added. The changes only make the existing text precise: (1) the localization is now the explicit Gabriel–Zisman formal-inverse localization, since the base citation of def-weil-abstract-derived-category only covers complexes in an abelian category; (2) the cone triangle is (f, i, -p), which matches def-weil-abstract-derived-category and Stacks 014E; (3) the balanced relation now reads b phi(c) ⊗ m = b ⊗ cm, where the base relation was ill-typed; (4) the derived extension is given by its universal property Nat(V, LF) ≅ Nat(V∘Q, F̄), which is exactly the right Kan extension (IsLeftDerivedFunctor), still conditional and asserting no existence; (5) the action counit is typed at Res N. I checked by hand: the shifted and cone Leibniz rules, d²=0, that d preserves the balanced relation using only that phi is a multiplicative chain map, that extension respects homotopies with H(b⊗m) = (-1)^{|b|} b⊗h(m), and that the counit map is balanced and C'-linear. Small cases: C=S in degree 0, f=0, the zero ring and empty space, phi=id, odd a with k=1. The citer lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-relative-flat-bar-extension (direction of the comparison map, its counit) and the parent def-sfb-dg-coefficient-realization agree with the delivered conventions.
